memories.author: D05
memories.text:
Diagnosis: Vitamin D deficiency, migraine without aura, and generalised anxiety disorder.
Patient reports fatigue, occasional frontal headaches, and worryfulness. Examination shows mild tenderness over frontal sinuses, no neurological deficits. Spirometry not indicated. Smoking status: never smoked, pack-years 0. Vitamin D replacement initiated, migraine prophylaxis started, anxiety treatment begun. Review in 3 months with labs and symptom diary.

memories.author: D05
memories.text:
cholecalciferol 60000 IU once weekly for 8 weeks, then 1000 IU OD
propranolol 40 mg OD
sumatriptan 50 mg SOS
topiramate 25 mg HS
escitalopram 5 mg OD
buspirone 5 mg BD

memories.author: D05
memories.text: CT head (non‑contrast): No acute intracranial pathology; ventricles and sulci normal for age.

memories.author: D05
memories.text:
Diagnosis: Vitamin D deficiency improving, migraine controlled, generalised anxiety disorder stable.
Patient feels less fatigued, headaches reduced to 1‑2 per month, reports better sleep. Examination: vitals stable, no focal neurology. Smoking status: never. Spirometry not required. Vitamin D now sufficient; continue maintenance dose. Migraine prophylaxis effective; consider adding acute NSAID. Anxiety improved, GAD‑7 8. Review in 3 months.

memories.author: patient
memories.text: I’ve noticed that sumatriptan sometimes gives me a tight feeling in my chest after I take it, though it helps the headache. I’m worried because I have a history of hypertension (well controlled). Could we try something else for acute migraine attacks? Also, I’ve been feeling a bit more anxious lately when driving in heavy traffic around Whitefield.

memories.author: D05
memories.text:
cholecalciferol 1000 IU OD
propranolol 40 mg OD
sumatriptan 50 mg SOS (to be used with caution, monitor chest symptoms)
rizatriptan 10 mg SOS (alternative if chest tightness recurs)
topiramate 50 mg HS
escitalopram 10 mg OD
buspirone 5 mg BD
naproxen 500 mg SOS (for migraine analgesia, avoid if GI upset)

memories.author: D05
memories.text:
Diagnosis: Vitamin D deficiency maintained, migraine well‑controlled, generalised anxiety disorder stable.
Patient reports no chest tightness with rizatriptan, headaches down to <1 per month. Driving anxiety improved with continued buspirone and escitalopram. Examination: vitals normal, no neurological signs. Smoking status: never. Spirometry not indicated. Continue current regimen; review in 6 months.
